diagnosis: The dispatch rule registration endpoint allows users to specify an arbitrary Redis pub/sub channel_pattern to fan out to an external target_url. Because it fails to validate that rule.channel_pattern is restricted to the caller's tenant namespace, an attacker can configure webhooks that tap into other tenants' private channels (e.g. tenant:enterprise_bank:wire_transfers:*), exfiltrating sensitive messages to an external server.

corrected_code:
@router.post("/notifications/dispatch-rules")
async def create_dispatch_rule(
    rule: DispatchRuleCreate,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)
):
    required_prefix = f"tenant:{current_user.tenant_id}:"
    if not rule.channel_pattern.startswith(required_prefix) and not current_user.is_system_admin:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Forbidden: channel pattern must be scoped to your tenant prefix")

    new_rule = DispatchRule(
        channel_pattern=rule.channel_pattern,
        target_url=rule.target_url,
        owner_id=current_user.id
    )
    db.add(new_rule)
    await db.commit()
    await db.refresh(new_rule)
    return new_rule
